Wizja uczyniona w Trąbczynie i przyległościach należących jako to w Nowej Wsi, Osinach, Łazach, i Olędrach budynków dworskich, jako tesz i wiejskich dnia 9 Lipca, roku Pańskiego 1754.
Dwor stary w Trąmpczynie z gruntu zły jak ściany tak dach ze wszystkiem który się reparować żadną miarą nie da.
Dwor nowy z rąb skończony dachem z jednej strony częścią alias dachówką położony reszta snopkami posproszy dwa pokoiki skończone nie ze wszystkiem, kumin jeden na wirzch wywiedziony do okien ramy wszystkie gotowe i futra takiej drzwi
Kuchnia przy tym dworze z rąb ze wszystkiem o dwuch izbach i spiżarnią z kozłami lecz nie pobita ani poszyta.
Stodoły poge od dworu nowego w gumna jest.
Stodoła po lewej ręce o jednym bojowisku z dylów łupanych w słupy nowa stawiana z wrotami obojmi
Druga stodoła w rogu pierwszy[m] dobra jak nowa w wiązanie stawiona cieślą z dylików rżniętych pirzona z dwojgiem wrót i fortką z jednej strony we sradku od dołu trzema szarami szkudeł pobita.
Trzecia stodoła w rogu tejże drugi z dylów łupanych w słupy stawiona o jednym bojowisku który upadają ku ziemię tylko że są po podpierane.
Czwarta tukasz i tyta także upadająca na ziemię
Owczarnia przy tych stodołach wielka od wirzchu w wiązaniej lepianką stawiana od dołu dylikami rżniętami pierzona ze wszystkiem w notami fortkami dobra om~a szarami szkudeł od dołu pobita i szczyty tarcicami pozabijane
Spichrz między temi stodołami niewielki o dwóch piętrach stary w lepianką w ktorym przyciesi pogniłej ściany po wyprężone a prawie z gruntu zły.
Chlewy Wozownia od powozow z dylow łupanych w słupy stawiona stara
Za tą wozownią Swynskię chlewy z dylow w słupy stare.
Obora dla bydla za temi chlewami z dylow łupanych w słupy stawiana dawna
Stania dla gosci przy wozowni z dylow w słupy stawiana pohilone [pochylone] sciany ku ogrodowi Stara
Staienka druga na wozowe konie Panskie w słupy a dyle łupane stawiane Stare
Stania dla koni cugowych z dylow lupanych w słupy stawiana dawna Snopkami poszyta i insze budynki wysze
Kup dla ruczenia wieprzy w dyla łupane nie wielki dwiema szarami szkudeł pobity.
Gorzalnia od wódki palonia izba z dylów rżniętych, sien w lepianką pruską roboty, komora przy sieni z balików rżniętych z drzwiami ze dworu, druga komora za izbą także z balików z rżniętych z drzwiami z izby, ze dworu drugiemi, szkudłami pobity cały budynek dobry. W Tej Gorzalni Garce do[20.?] jeden większy drugi mniejszy z pokrywami rurumi dobremi rurnicami kłodami do zacieru z bejką do [?][?]gru konwiami wybirkami staremi.
Mielcuch wielki nie bardzo izba jedna w blochy stara przyciesi podwleczone pod nię sień do piwa robienia w lepiankę w tej sieni suszenie dolne dobre z piecem murowanym w cegłę za tym suszeniem jest Izba w blochy nieskończona ze wszystkiem z tej izby komory 2. z drzwiami jednemi z izby z jedny do drugi z tej sieni drzwi do sklepu do piwa schowania za tym sklepem komora do schowania z tej sieni schody na gorę nad izbą od wrót na który sypanie jest, na polowie zas drugi mielcucha nieskończony posowy nie masz drzwi ani okien Kamin lepiony, w tym kuminie kociolek niewielki zabierujący beczek 3. wody stary łatany, kadzie z[?] dobre Trybusek 1, beczek 20, i insze statki ktore są potrzebne do Mielcucha szkudłami cały budynek niedawno pobity szczyty tarcicami obydwa zabyte.
Wieś Nowa:
Olędrów 15 szesnasta huba próżna jedni się pobudowali dobrze drudzy tylko budy w ziemi mają.
Spisanie ludzi zaciężnych w Trąbczynie
Kmieć 4 ma z nich każdy bydła do roboty 8 pańskiego wołów 4 koni 4 krowy 2 wozy 2 świnie żelaza wszystkie jak się należy i zasiewki oboje tak ozimie jako i jare.
Półrolników 5 ma z nich każdy bydła do roboty Pańskiego 4 krowę, świnię, wół, żelaza wszystkie jak się należy i zasi[e]wki oboje.
Chałupników 7 ci nie mają pańskiego bydła
Komornic wszystkich 8.
w Osinach
Kmieć 1 tak ma jak i Trąbczyński wszystko
Półrolników 2 tak mają jak Trąbczynscy
Chałupników 2
Komornic 3
w Lazach
Kmieć 1 tak ma zaprzęg jak i insi
Chałupników 3
w Nowey wsi
Półrolników 2 jeden ma bydło wszystko a drugi tylko do roboty ma 3
Chałupników 2
Komornik 1
Hatew w który mieszkają ludzie to jest chłopów lecz ci nie robią ani tesz Pańskiego nie mają.
Niżej wyrażeni zeznajemy z woźnym Bartłomiejem będąc na wizji borów Trąbczyńskich ciągnących się od Osin nad granicami Drzewieckiemi, iż widzieliśmy że sosień co lepsze i piękniejsze a najbardziej nimo słupa i przychodu kniejów nazywających się połowa większa wycięta jest aż ku Łomowu od Łomowa zaś poprzebierane są co piękniejsze sosny aż ku granicom Biskupskim, zaś od Biskupskich granic i przed Czarnem Brodem i za brodem nad Szetlejowkiem ku Łazom same tylko wybirki stoją z których nie wybierze nic na budynek, zaś nimo Łazów i Osin między Hutą gdzie najpiękniejsze drzewo było i tam powycinane same też wybirki stoją. Także i dęby w lasach stojące dotychczas same też wybirki stoją tylko gdyż Olędry pozabierali hubami gdzie pieknięjsze drzewo było wydzielonymi z dawna każdemu z nich czego dla utwierdzenia i lepszej wiary rękami własnymi podpisujemy się. Działo się w Trąbczynie dnia 9 Julii Anno Domini 1754.
Kazimirz Swierczewski manu propria
Józef Puchalski manu propria
In Conin Feria Sexta pridie Festi Sanctae Margarithae Virginis et Martyris Anno Domini 1754
Ad officium et acta praesentia Castrensia Coniensia personaliter veniens Ministerialis Regni Generalis Providus Bartholomaeus Szeptycki [Szepczyński] de Trąmpczyn officio praesenti notus sanus existens recognovit quia ipse habitis secum Nobilibus Generosis Casimiro Swierczewski et Josepho Puchalski hic licet ad praesens absentibus in loco tamen negotii infrascripti pro tunc praesentibus ad instantiam et officiosam requisitionem Magnificae Catharinae de Rozdrazewskie Prusimska olim Magnifici Pauli Prusimski Succamerarii suae Regiae Majestatis non pridem vita functi Bonorum Trąmpczyn cum attinentiis Haeredis Consortis Relictae viduae ab eodemque olim Magnifico Marito suo in Bonis eius omnibus Dominae Reformatoriae et advitalitialis Feria Tertia proxime et Immediate condescenderat personaliter ad Bona eadem Trąmpczyn principaliter tum villas Osiny, Lazy, Nowa Wieś, Olędry i Chuta attinentes tum Borras ac Sylvas ad eadem Bona spectantes Ibidemque ubique eorundem Locorum Successive existens iuxta Iuris et Consuetudinis formam vidit ac debite conspexit utpote Inseratur Quae praemissa se debite vidisse et conspexisse coram eodem officio attestatus de quo hanc sui Relationem fecit facitque praesentem.

Niżej wyrażeni zeznajemy z woźnym Bartłomiejem będąc na wizji borów Trąbczyńskich ciągnących się od Osin nad granicami Drzewieckiemi, iż widzieliśmy że sosień co lepsze i piękniejsze a najbardziej nimo słupa i przychodu kniejów nazywających się połowa większa wycięta jest aż ku Łomowu od Łomowa zaś poprzebierane są co piękniejsze sosny aż ku granicom Biskupskim, zaś od Biskupskich granic i przed Czarnem Brodem i za brodem nad Szetlejowkiem ku Łazom same tylko wybirki stoją z których nie wybierze nic na budynek, zaś nimo Łazów i Osin między Hutą gdzie najpiękniejsze drzewo było i tam powycinane same też wybirki stoją. Także i dęby w lasach stojące dotychczas same też wybirki stoją tylko gdyż Olędry pozabierali hubami gdzie pieknięjsze drzewo było wydzielonymi z dawna każdemu z nich czego dla utwierdzenia i lepszej wiary rękami własnymi podpisujemy się. Działo się w Trąbczynie dnia 9 Julii Anno Domini 1754.

In Conin Feria Sexta pridie Festi Sanctae Margarithae Virginis et Martyris Anno Domini 1754

translation.en:
Judicial site inspection conducted in Trąbczyn and its adjacent appurtenances, namely in Nowa Wieś, Osiny, Łazy, and the olędry, of manorial buildings and likewise village ones, on 9 July in the year of the Lord 1754.

[Translator's note: Wizja as judicial site inspection. Rule 17 translates wizja as 'judicial site inspection' throughout. In this document the term covers two distinct uses: (1) the building and estate survey forming Section 1, which is an administrative inventory conducted at the instance of the widowed proprietress rather than a court-ordered boundary inspection in the sense of the 1776 proceedings; and (2) the forest inspection forming Section 3, formally witnessed, signed, and registered at the municipal court three days later. Both are translated as 'judicial site inspection' per Rule 17; the different character of Section 1 is noted here.]

The old manor in Trąbczyn is thoroughly bad — both walls and roof with everything — which can by no means be repaired.

The new manor, of hewn log construction, finished — the roof on one side laid in part, that is, with roof tiles, the remainder lightly strewn with bundles of thatch — two small rooms finished, though not entirely; one chimney carried to the top; frames ready for all windows; and casings for such doors.

[Translator's note: 'Hewn log construction.' Z rąb, genitive plural of rąb (a hewn or notched log; squared timber). A log-frame technique using hewn timbers rather than sawn planks or earthen infill. Distinct from framed construction (w wiązaniu) and daub construction (w lepianką) used elsewhere in this survey.]

[Translator's note: 'Lightly strewn with bundles of thatch.' Snopkami posproszy, past passive participle from prószyć (to strew or scatter thinly), with po- prefix. The grammatical agreement with reszta (the remainder, feminine) is irregular in the source. The sense is a roof surface loosely covered with straw bundles — a temporary or provisional covering — as opposed to the properly laid tiles on the other side.]

[Translator's note: 'Casings for such doors.' Futra takiej drzwi. Futro (a door or window casing; the wooden surround fitted to a prepared opening). Takiej drzwi is a scribal case variant of takich drzwi (of such doors). The passage lists ramy (frames) for windows and futra (casings) for doors as the items ready for fitting — both implying the openings are prepared but not yet hung or glazed.]

The kitchen at this manor, of hewn log construction, complete in every respect, of two rooms and a pantry with sawhorses, but not boarded nor thatched.

[Translator's note: 'Sawhorses.' Z kozłami. Kozły (sawhorses, trestles, or roof trusses) in a building context; here possibly referring to roof trusses or construction supports.]

The barns are [away] from the new manor, in the farmyard.

[Translator's note: '[Away].' Poge is an unresolved reading in the source transcription. The most contextually plausible sense is 'away from' or 'at some distance from,' locating the barn complex away from the manor house proper. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

[Translator's note: Farmyard. Gumno (the threshing yard or farmyard; the enclosed service yard of a noble estate comprising the barn complex, threshing floors, and related agricultural outbuildings). Distinct from the manor house precinct.]

Barn on the left, of one threshing floor, of split planks into posts, newly built, with both gates.

The second barn in the first corner, good as new, built in framed construction by a carpenter, of small sawn planks, [fitted], with double gates and a wicket gate on one side; in the middle, covered from below with three courses of shingles.

[Translator's note: '[Fitted].' Pirzona (second barn) and pierzona (sheepfold) are the same or near-identical word appearing twice. No confident reconstruction has been established; the word likely denotes some finishing treatment, lining, or fitting of the plank cladding. Translated tentatively as '[fitted]' in both occurrences. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

[Translator's note: Shingles. Szkudła (singular szkudła), from German Schindel: thin wooden roofing tiles. Szarami is rendered as 'courses' — probably from German Schar (a row or course of roofing material), denoting horizontal layers in which shingles are laid. The term szary in this sense is not attested in standard Polish dictionaries and may be a regional or trade term.]

The third barn in the second corner of the same, of split planks into posts, built of one threshing floor — [the walls of which] are collapsing to the ground, only that they are propped.

The fourth, likewise also collapsing to the ground.

[Translator's note: 'The fourth, likewise also collapsing to the ground.' Czwarta tukasz i tyta także upadająca na ziemię. The words tukasz i tyta are unresolved in the source. The most plausible reading is tudzież i ta (likewise and that one also), producing 'the fourth, likewise that one also collapsing.' The translation follows this reading. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

The sheepfold at these barns, large, built from the top in framed daub construction, from below with small sawn planks, [fitted] in every respect, with [new] gates, good, [moss-covered], covered with courses of shingles from below; and both gables fastened with boards.

[Translator's note: Daub. Lepianka (wattle-and-daub or earthen-infill construction; from lepić, to mould or plaster). Lepianka pruska (Prussian daub; pruska roboty, of Prussian construction) denotes a half-timber or Fachwerk technique using a timber frame with clay infill, common in Greater Poland in this period. In the Owczarnia (sheepfold) passage, the upper section is framed daub (w wiązaniej lepianką) and the lower section is clad with small sawn planks.]

[Translator's note: '[Fitted].' Pirzona (second barn) and pierzona (sheepfold) are the same or near-identical word appearing twice. No confident reconstruction has been established; the word likely denotes some finishing treatment, lining, or fitting of the plank cladding. Translated tentatively as '[fitted]' in both occurrences. The manuscript requires re-examination.]

[Translator's note: '[New] gates.' W notami fortkami. Fortkami is instrumental plural of fortka (wicket gate; a small gate): the reading is clear. Notami is uncertain — possibly a misread of nowymi (new, instrumental plural), giving 'with new gates.' The preposition w may also be a misread of z (with). Translated tentatively as '[new] gates.']

[Translator's note: '[Moss-covered].' Om~a: a contracted form, the tilde indicating a suspension. The most likely expansion is omszała or omszona (moss-covered; weathered with age). Translated tentatively; the manuscript requires re-examination.]

The granary between these barns — small, of two storeys, old, in daub construction, in which the sill beams are rotted, the walls pushed out, and indeed thoroughly bad.

Outbuildings. The carriage house for carriages, of split planks into posts, built, old.

[Translator's note: 'Outbuildings.' Chlewy (pigsties; also used loosely as a generic term for farm outbuildings) appears to function here as a section heading introducing the series of service buildings that follows — the carriage house, pig sties, cowshed, stables, and pen. The specific pig sties (Świńskie chlewy) behind the carriage house are then identified separately in the next entry.]

Behind that carriage house, pig sties of planks into posts, old.

A cowshed for cattle behind those pigsties, of split planks into posts, built, of old construction.

Guest stables at the carriage house, of planks into posts, built, walls leaning toward the garden, old.

[Translator's note: 'Walls leaning toward the garden.' Pohilone ściany ku ogrodowi. Pohilone = pochylone (leaning, tilted), with h for ch and i for y, consistent with this hand. The garden-facing walls of the guest stables are structurally compromised.]

A second small stable for the lord's carriage horses, of posts and split planks, built, old.

Stables for draught-team horses, of split planks into posts, built, of old construction, thatched with bundles; and other buildings above.

[Translator's note: Draught-team horses. Konie cugowe, from cug (German Zug: a carriage team or draught team). Distinguished in the survey from konie wozowe (the lord's personal carriage horses) in the preceding entry. The two stables serve animals of different function and rank.]

[Translator's note: 'Other buildings above.' I insze budynki wyże: a summary phrase indicating further structures enumerated in the preceding text. The passage closes the outbuilding inventory.]

A pen for pigs, of split plank, not large, covered with two courses of shingles.

[Translator's note: 'Pen for pigs.' Kup dla ruczenia wieprzy. Kup (pen, sty). Ruczenia is uncertain — possibly dialectal from rucić (to cast or throw) or from ruch (movement, roaming). Translated as 'for pigs' as a working rendering; the structure houses boars (wieprze) for fattening or keeping.]

The distillery for [-----] vodka: a room of sawn planks; the vestibule in Prussian daub construction; a storeroom next to the vestibule of small sawn planks, with a door from outside; a second storeroom behind the room likewise of small sawn planks, with a door from the room and a second from outside — the entire building good, covered with shingles. In this distillery: still-pots — one larger, one smaller — with covers, good pipes, condenser fittings, mash tubs, a barrel for a distillation run, buckets, old ladles.

[Translator's note: [-----]. Palonia remains unresolved in the source. Two readings have been proposed: (1) palona (heated, fired), describing the still-room as the fired or heated space of the distillery; (2) a qualifier of wódki (vodka), possibly indicating a specific type such as Polish-style vodka. Neither has been confirmed from the manuscript. Left untranslated pending resolution.]

[Translator's note: Prussian daub. See note [^12].]

[Translator's note: Still-pots. Garce (singular garc: a vessel or pot used in the distilling apparatus, probably from German Gar or a related term). The number in the source (do [20.?]) is uncertain in the manuscript; it may read as 'two' (dwa) or as a capacity or count figure. The two pots described — one larger, one smaller — may be the garc vessels themselves.]

[Translator's note: Condenser fittings. Rurnicami: a technical term for components of the distilling condenser or pipe fittings. The exact meaning is uncertain; possibly from rurnik (one who works with pipes or condenser tubes).]

[Translator's note: Mash tubs. Kłodami do zacieru. Zacier is the mash — the mixture of grain and water fermented in the initial stage of vodka or beer production. Kłody are large wooden tubs or containers.]

[Translator's note: Distillation run. Do [??]gru: the word following do is incompletely legible in the manuscript. Przegon (a single pass of liquid through the still; a distillation run) is the most plausible candidate, giving 'a barrel for the distillation run.' Translated tentatively.]

[Translator's note: Ladles. Wybirkami: small scooping or ladling vessels, from wybierać (to scoop out; to ladle). Distinct from wybirki (selection remnants) in Section 3 — same root, different nominal form and meaning.]

The malthouse, large — not very: one room of log construction, old, sill beams dragged beneath it; the vestibule for brewing beer, of daub construction; in this vestibule a lower drying kiln, good, with a brick-built oven; behind this drying kiln there is a room of log construction, unfinished in every respect; from this room, two storerooms with one door from the room, from one to the other; from this vestibule, a door to the vault for storing beer; behind this vault, a storeroom for storage; from this vestibule, stairs upward above the room, from the gates — on which grain storage is made. On the second half of the malthouse, unfinished — no ceiling boards, doors, or windows; a clay-built chimney; in this chimney a small kettle holding three barrels of water, old, patched; vats, sufficiently good; one trivet; twenty barrels; and other vessels needed for the malthouse — the entire building recently covered with shingles, both gables fastened with boards.

[Translator's note: Malthouse. Mielcuch: a combined malthouse and brewery for producing malt and beer. A standard feature of larger Polish noble estates in this period.]

[Translator's note: Ceiling boards. Posowy: a technical term for the planks forming the ceiling or loft floor of a building, dividing an upper grain storage area from the rooms below. The unfinished half of the malthouse lacks these.]

[Translator's note: 'Sufficiently good.' Kadzie z[?] dobre. The word following z is unclear in the manuscript; dość (sufficiently) or zdatne (serviceable) are the most plausible candidates.]

[Translator's note: Trivet. Trybusek, from German Dreibuss: a three-legged stand placed over a fire for supporting cooking or distilling vessels.]

[The description of the village houses, one by one, which follows here on the rest of leaf 121 verso, on leaf 122 and at the top of leaf 122 verso, is not transcribed.]

[Section 2 — Tenant Enumeration]

Village of Nowa Wieś:

Fifteen olędry; the sixteenth plot empty. Some have built well, whereas others have only earth dugouts.

[Translator's note: 'Plot.' Huba, from German Hufe: the standard unit of land allocated to each olęder settler family. The 'sixteenth plot' (szesnasta huba) is vacant — one of the sixteen expected settler holdings is unoccupied.]

Enumeration of dependent people in Trąbczyn:

[Translator's note: Dependent people. Ludzie zaciężni: persons tied to the estate by obligation — serfs or bound tenants. The enumeration lists them by category in descending social and economic order.]

Full farmers: 4. Each of them has — working cattle: 8 of the lord's; oxen: 4; horses: 4; cows: 2; wagons: 2; pigs; ironware — all as is proper — and sowings both: winter grain and spring grain.

[Translator's note: Full farmers. Kmiecie (singular kmieć): the highest category of dependent peasant, holding a full farm unit and obligated to provide full labour services with a complete draught team.]

Half-farmers: 5. Each of them has — working cattle of the lord's: 4; a cow; a pig; an ox; ironware — all as is proper — and sowings both.

[Translator's note: Half-farmers. Półrolnicy (singular półrolnik): dependent peasants holding a half farm unit, with correspondingly reduced draught teams and labour obligations.]

Cottagers: 7. These have no lord's cattle.

[Translator's note: Cottagers. Chałupnicy (singular chałupnik): dependent peasants holding only a cottage and garden, with no arable land allocation and reduced labour obligations.]

Female lodgers: in all, 8.

[Translator's note: Lodgers. Komornicy / komornice (singular komornik / komornica): the most dependent category of rural resident, holding neither land nor a full cottage, typically lodging with another household. This use of komornik is entirely distinct from komornik graniczny (Boundary Surveyor) throughout the main project documents.]

In Osiny:

Full farmer: 1 — has all as the Trąbczyn [full farmer].

Half-farmers: 2 — have as the Trąbczyńskis.

Cottagers: 2.

Female lodgers: 3.

In Łazy:

Full farmer: 1 — has a team as the others.

Cottagers: 3.

In Nowa Wieś:

Half-farmers: 2 — one has all the cattle; the other has for work only 3.

Cottagers: 2.

Lodger: 1.

Cottages in which people live — that is, [free] peasants — but these do not perform labour obligations nor do they have the lord's cattle.

[Translator's note: Cottages. Chatew: a regional or period genitive plural form of chata (a simple peasant cottage or dwelling). The word governs w których mieszkają ludzie ('in which people live'); który in the source is a scribal case slip for których.]

[Translator's note: '[Free] peasants.' Chłopów (genitive plural of chłop): peasants who, notably, owe no labour obligations and hold no lord's cattle — indicating a distinct contractual or personal status from the bound tenants enumerated above. The word 'free' is supplied in brackets as an interpretive clarification; the source has only chłopów.]

[Translator's note: Labour obligations. Robota: obligatory serf labour owed by dependent peasants to the estate lord, typically measured as a set number of days of field work per week. The formulaic phrase nie robią ('they do not work') signals exemption from this obligation.]

[Section 3 — Forest Testimony]

The undersigned testify, together with the Court Summoner Bartłomiej, having been at the judicial site inspection of the Trąbczyn pine forests stretching from Osiny along the Drzewce boundaries — that we saw: that the pines, the better and finer ones, and most especially past the boundary post and at the approach of the thickets known as [-----], the larger half has been felled as far as Łomów. From Łomów, the finer pines have been selectively taken all the way to the Biskupice boundaries; and from the Biskupice boundaries — both before czarny bród and beyond the ford, above Szetlewek toward Łazy — only selection remnants stand, from which nothing can be chosen for building. And likewise past Łazy and Osiny, between the Huta, where the finest timber was — there too, felled, only selection remnants stand. Likewise the oaks standing in the woodlands — to this day only selection remnants stand — only because the olędry took [the timber] from the plots long since allocated to each of them, where the finer timber was. In witness and confirmation of this we sign with our own hands. Done in Trąbczyn on 9 July in the year of the Lord 1754.

[Translator's note: 'At the approach of the thickets.' Przy przychodu kniejów: przychód (approach, entry-point); knieje (thickets; dense sections of woodland). The preposition nimo (past, alongside — a variant of mimo) governs both słupa (the boundary post) and przychodu kniejów (the approach of the thickets), reading: 'past the boundary post and past the approach of the thickets.']

[Translator's note: [-----]. The name or descriptor of the thickets (nazywających się — 'known as [X]') appears to be absent or illegible in the manuscript at this point.]

[Translator's note: 'Selectively taken.' Poprzebierane: past passive participle of przebierać (to pick through; to select the best and leave the rest). The word describes selective logging — the finest trees removed, the lesser ones left.]

[Translator's note: Selection remnants. Wybirki: from wybierać (to select, to pick out). Trees or timber remaining after selective felling — those not considered worth taking. The word appears three times in the forest testimony. See also note [^26]: the same verbal root yields wybirkami (ladles) in Section 1, a different nominal form with a different meaning.]

[Translator's note: Huta. The glassworks on the Trąbczyn estate. A glassworks (huta szklana) consumed large quantities of timber as fuel and raw material, explaining its association with the depletion of fine forest. The Huta appears in the Latin registration record below as Chuta, with Ch- for H- as a Latin orthographic convention. It is also mentioned in the 1776 commission document as the destination of timber illegally felled from the Trąbczyn woodlands by the Chełmski predecessors.]

[Translator's note: 'Plots.' Hubami: instrumental plural of huba. The olędry had received specific land allocations including wooded portions; they had taken the finest timber from within their own allocated plots.]

Kazimierz Świerczewski, by his own hand

Józef Puchalski, by his own hand

[Section 4 — Registration Record]

In Konin, on Friday, the eve of the Feast of Saint Margaret, Virgin and Martyr, 12 July 1754.

Before the present records and acts of the Konin Starost's Municipal Court, appearing in person — the General Court Summoner of the Realm, the Honest Bartłomiej Szeptycki [Szepczyński] of Trąbczyn, known to the present office, being of sound mind — declared: having with him the Honourables Kasimierz Świerczewski and Józef Puchalski — who, although at present absent [from the court], were at the time present at the place of the matter described below — at the instance and official requisition of the Right Honourable Katarzyna Prusimska of Rozdrażew, surviving widow of the late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, Sub-chamberlain of His Royal Majesty, not long since deceased — hereditary lady and consort of the Trąbczyn estate with its appurtenances, and by the said late husband endowed with life-tenure and dower in all his goods — on Tuesday immediately preceding had made a formal descent in person to the same Trąbczyn estate first, then to the villages of Osiny, Łazy, Nowa Wieś, the olędry, and the Huta belonging to it, then to the pine forests and woodlands pertaining to those same goods; and being everywhere throughout those same places in succession, in accordance with the form of law and custom, had duly viewed and inspected — to be entered as follows. Which aforesaid matters he attested before the said office as having duly viewed and inspected — of which he made and makes this his report in the present act.

[Translator's note: Szeptycki [Szepczyński]. Bartłomiej is named Szeptycki in this 1754 record and Szepczyński in the 1782 document; in the 1776 document he is uczciwy Bartłomi z Trąpczyna (the Honest Bartłomiej of Trąbczyn). All three designations refer to the same individual, who served as Court Summoner of Trąbczyn across at least the period 1754–1782. The variant spellings are preserved as written in their respective documents.]

[Translator's note: Life-tenure and dower. Dominae Reformatoriae et advitalitialis (Latin). Reformatoria denotes the right of a widow to reform or reclaim her dower on the death of her husband, a standard provision of Polish noble inheritance law. Advitalis denotes a life interest or life tenancy in the goods. Katarzyna Prusimska thus held both a dower-reform right and a life tenancy in all of Paweł Prusimski's goods.]

[Translator's note: Formal descent. Condescenderat (Latin, pluperfect of condescendere): a technical legal term denoting the formal act of proceeding to an estate for an official on-site inspection. The Tuesday in question was 9 July 1754 — three days before the registration on 12 July 1754 (the eve of the Feast of Saint Margaret, Virgin and Martyr).]

[Translator's note: 'To be entered as follows.' Utpote Inseratur (Latin): a formulaic note indicating that the content of the inspection — that is, Sections 1–3 above — is to be inserted into the court record at this point. The three Polish sections (building survey, tenant enumeration, and forest testimony) are thus the material being formally registered by this relatio.]

Notami is uncertain — possibly a misread of nowymi (new, instrumental plural), giving 'with new gates.' The preposition w may also be a misread of z (with). Translated tentatively as '[new] gates.']

[Translator's note: '[Moss-covered].' Om~a: a contracted form, the tilde indicating a suspension. The most likely expansion is omszała or omszona (moss-covered; weathered with age). Translated tentatively; the manuscript requires re-examination.]

The granary between these barns — small, of two storeys, old, in daub construction, in which the sill beams are rotted, the walls pushed out, and indeed thoroughly bad.

Outbuildings. The carriage house for carriages, of split planks into posts, built, old.

[Translator's note: 'Outbuildings.' Chlewy (pigsties; also used loosely as a generic term for farm outbuildings) appears to function here as a section heading introducing the series of service buildings that follows — the carriage house, pig sties, cowshed, stables, and pen. The specific pig sties (Świńskie chlewy) behind the carriage house are then identified separately in the next entry.]

Behind that carriage house, pig sties of planks into posts, old.

A cowshed for cattle behind those pigsties, of split planks into posts, built, of old construction.

Guest stables at the carriage house, of planks into posts, built, walls leaning toward the garden, old.

[Translator's note: 'Walls leaning toward the garden.' Pohilone ściany ku ogrodowi. Pohilone = pochylone (leaning, tilted), with h for ch and i for y, consistent with this hand. The garden-facing walls of the guest stables are structurally compromised.]

A second small stable for the lord's carriage horses, of posts and split planks, built, old.

Stables for draught-team horses, of split planks into posts, built, of old construction, thatched with bundles; and other buildings above.

[Translator's note: Draught-team horses. Konie cugowe, from cug (German Zug: a carriage team or draught team). Distinguished in the survey from konie wozowe (the lord's personal carriage horses) in the preceding entry. The two stables serve animals of different function and rank.]

[Translator's note: 'Other buildings above.' I insze budynki wyże: a summary phrase indicating further structures enumerated in the preceding text. The passage closes the outbuilding inventory.]

A pen for pigs, of split plank, not large, covered with two courses of shingles.

[Translator's note: 'Pen for pigs.' Kup dla ruczenia wieprzy. Kup (pen, sty). Ruczenia is uncertain — possibly dialectal from rucić (to cast or throw) or from ruch (movement, roaming). Translated as 'for pigs' as a working rendering; the structure houses boars (wieprze) for fattening or keeping.]

The distillery for [-----] vodka: a room of sawn planks; the vestibule in Prussian daub construction; a storeroom next to the vestibule of small sawn planks, with a door from outside; a second storeroom behind the room likewise of small sawn planks, with a door from the room and a second from outside — the entire building good, covered with shingles. In this distillery: still-pots — one larger, one smaller — with covers, good pipes, condenser fittings, mash tubs, a barrel for a distillation run, buckets, old ladles.

[Translator's note: [-----]. Palonia remains unresolved in the source. Two readings have been proposed: (1) palona (heated, fired), describing the still-room as the fired or heated space of the distillery; (2) a qualifier of wódki (vodka), possibly indicating a specific type such as Polish-style vodka. Neither has been confirmed from the manuscript. Left untranslated pending resolution.]

[Translator's note: Prussian daub. See note [^12].]

[Translator's note: Still-pots. Garce (singular garc: a vessel or pot used in the distilling apparatus, probably from German Gar or a related term). The number in the source (do [20.?]) is uncertain in the manuscript; it may read as 'two' (dwa) or as a capacity or count figure. The two pots described — one larger, one smaller — may be the garc vessels themselves.]

[Translator's note: Condenser fittings. Rurnicami: a technical term for components of the distilling condenser or pipe fittings. The exact meaning is uncertain; possibly from rurnik (one who works with pipes or condenser tubes).]

[Translator's note: Mash tubs. Kłodami do zacieru. Zacier is the mash — the mixture of grain and water fermented in the initial stage of vodka or beer production. Kłody are large wooden tubs or containers.]

[Translator's note: Distillation run. Do [??]gru: the word following do is incompletely legible in the manuscript. Przegon (a single pass of liquid through the still; a distillation run) is the most plausible candidate, giving 'a barrel for the distillation run.' Translated tentatively.]

[Translator's note: Ladles. Wybirkami: small scooping or ladling vessels, from wybierać (to scoop out; to ladle). Distinct from wybirki (selection remnants) in Section 3 — same root, different nominal form and meaning.]

The malthouse, large — not very: one room of log construction, old, sill beams dragged beneath it; the vestibule for brewing beer, of daub construction; in this vestibule a lower drying kiln, good, with a brick-built oven; behind this drying kiln there is a room of log construction, unfinished in every respect; from this room, two storerooms with one door from the room, from one to the other; from this vestibule, a door to the vault for storing beer; behind this vault, a storeroom for storage; from this vestibule, stairs upward above the room, from the gates — on which grain storage is made. On the second half of the malthouse, unfinished — no ceiling boards, doors, or windows; a clay-built chimney; in this chimney a small kettle holding three barrels of water, old, patched; vats, sufficiently good; one trivet; twenty barrels; and other vessels needed for the malthouse — the entire building recently covered with shingles, both gables fastened with boards.

[Translator's note: Malthouse. Mielcuch: a combined malthouse and brewery for producing malt and beer. A standard feature of larger Polish noble estates in this period.]

[Translator's note: Ceiling boards. Posowy: a technical term for the planks forming the ceiling or loft floor of a building, dividing an upper grain storage area from the rooms below. The unfinished half of the malthouse lacks these.]

[Translator's note: 'Sufficiently good.' Kadzie z[?] dobre. The word following z is unclear in the manuscript; dość (sufficiently) or zdatne (serviceable) are the most plausible candidates.]

[Translator's note: Trivet. Trybusek, from German Dreibuss: a three-legged stand placed over a fire for supporting cooking or distilling vessels.]

[The description of the village houses, one by one, which follows here on the rest of leaf 121 verso, on leaf 122 and at the top of leaf 122 verso, is not transcribed.]

[Section 2 — Tenant Enumeration]

Village of Nowa Wieś:

Fifteen olędry; the sixteenth plot empty. Some have built well, whereas others have only earth dugouts.

[Translator's note: 'Plot.' Huba, from German Hufe: the standard unit of land allocated to each olęder settler family. The 'sixteenth plot' (szesnasta huba) is vacant — one of the sixteen expected settler holdings is unoccupied.]

Enumeration of dependent people in Trąbczyn:

[Translator's note: Dependent people. Ludzie zaciężni: persons tied to the estate by obligation — serfs or bound tenants. The enumeration lists them by category in descending social and economic order.]

Full farmers: 4. Each of them has — working cattle: 8 of the lord's; oxen: 4; horses: 4; cows: 2; wagons: 2; pigs; ironware — all as is proper — and sowings both: winter grain and spring grain.

[Translator's note: Full farmers. Kmiecie (singular kmieć): the highest category of dependent peasant, holding a full farm unit and obligated to provide full labour services with a complete draught team.]

Half-farmers: 5. Each of them has — working cattle of the lord's: 4; a cow; a pig; an ox; ironware — all as is proper — and sowings both.

[Translator's note: Half-farmers. Półrolnicy (singular półrolnik): dependent peasants holding a half farm unit, with correspondingly reduced draught teams and labour obligations.]

Cottagers: 7. These have no lord's cattle.

[Translator's note: Cottagers. Chałupnicy (singular chałupnik): dependent peasants holding only a cottage and garden, with no arable land allocation and reduced labour obligations.]

Female lodgers: in all, 8.

[Translator's note: Lodgers. Komornicy / komornice (singular komornik / komornica): the most dependent category of rural resident, holding neither land nor a full cottage, typically lodging with another household. This use of komornik is entirely distinct from komornik graniczny (Boundary Surveyor) throughout the main project documents.]

In Osiny:

Full farmer: 1 — has all as the Trąbczyn [full farmer].

Half-farmers: 2 — have as the Trąbczyńskis.

Cottagers: 2.

Female lodgers: 3.

In Łazy:

Full farmer: 1 — has a team as the others.

Cottagers: 3.

In Nowa Wieś:

Half-farmers: 2 — one has all the cattle; the other has for work only 3.

Cottagers: 2.

Lodger: 1.

Cottages in which people live — that is, [free] peasants — but these do not perform labour obligations nor do they have the lord's cattle.

[Translator's note: Cottages. Chatew: a regional or period genitive plural form of chata (a simple peasant cottage or dwelling). The word governs w których mieszkają ludzie ('in which people live'); który in the source is a scribal case slip for których.]

[Translator's note: '[Free] peasants.' Chłopów (genitive plural of chłop): peasants who, notably, owe no labour obligations and hold no lord's cattle — indicating a distinct contractual or personal status from the bound tenants enumerated above. The word 'free' is supplied in brackets as an interpretive clarification; the source has only chłopów.]

[Translator's note: Labour obligations. Robota: obligatory serf labour owed by dependent peasants to the estate lord, typically measured as a set number of days of field work per week. The formulaic phrase nie robią ('they do not work') signals exemption from this obligation.]

[Section 3 — Forest Testimony]

The undersigned testify, together with the Court Summoner Bartłomiej, having been at the judicial site inspection of the Trąbczyn pine forests stretching from Osiny along the Drzewce boundaries — that we saw: that the pines, the better and finer ones, and most especially past the boundary post and at the approach of the thickets known as [-----], the larger half has been felled as far as Łomów. From Łomów, the finer pines have been selectively taken all the way to the Biskupice boundaries; and from the Biskupice boundaries — both before czarny bród and beyond the ford, above Szetlewek toward Łazy — only selection remnants stand, from which nothing can be chosen for building. And likewise past Łazy and Osiny, between the Huta, where the finest timber was — there too, felled, only selection remnants stand. Likewise the oaks standing in the woodlands — to this day only selection remnants stand — only because the olędry took [the timber] from the plots long since allocated to each of them, where the finer timber was. In witness and confirmation of this we sign with our own hands. Done in Trąbczyn on 9 July in the year of the Lord 1754.

[Translator's note: 'At the approach of the thickets.' Przy przychodu kniejów: przychód (approach, entry-point); knieje (thickets; dense sections of woodland). The preposition nimo (past, alongside — a variant of mimo) governs both słupa (the boundary post) and przychodu kniejów (the approach of the thickets), reading: 'past the boundary post and past the approach of the thickets.']

[Translator's note: [-----]. The name or descriptor of the thickets (nazywających się — 'known as [X]') appears to be absent or illegible in the manuscript at this point.]

[Translator's note: 'Selectively taken.' Poprzebierane: past passive participle of przebierać (to pick through; to select the best and leave the rest). The word describes selective logging — the finest trees removed, the lesser ones left.]

[Translator's note: Selection remnants. Wybirki: from wybierać (to select, to pick out). Trees or timber remaining after selective felling — those not considered worth taking. The word appears three times in the forest testimony. See also note [^26]: the same verbal root yields wybirkami (ladles) in Section 1, a different nominal form with a different meaning.]

[Translator's note: Huta. The glassworks on the Trąbczyn estate. A glassworks (huta szklana) consumed large quantities of timber as fuel and raw material, explaining its association with the depletion of fine forest. The Huta appears in the Latin registration record below as Chuta, with Ch- for H- as a Latin orthographic convention. It is also mentioned in the 1776 commission document as the destination of timber illegally felled from the Trąbczyn woodlands by the Chełmski predecessors.]

[Translator's note: 'Plots.' Hubami: instrumental plural of huba. The olędry had received specific land allocations including wooded portions; they had taken the finest timber from within their own allocated plots.]

Kazimierz Świerczewski, by his own hand

Józef Puchalski, by his own hand

[Section 4 — Registration Record]

In Konin, on Friday, the eve of the Feast of Saint Margaret, Virgin and Martyr, 12 July 1754.

Before the present records and acts of the Konin Starost's Municipal Court, appearing in person — the General Court Summoner of the Realm, the Honest Bartłomiej Szeptycki [Szepczyński] of Trąbczyn, known to the present office, being of sound mind — declared: having with him the Honourables Kasimierz Świerczewski and Józef Puchalski — who, although at present absent [from the court], were at the time present at the place of the matter described below — at the instance and official requisition of the Right Honourable Katarzyna Prusimska of Rozdrażew, surviving widow of the late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, Sub-chamberlain of His Royal Majesty, not long since deceased — hereditary lady and consort of the Trąbczyn estate with its appurtenances, and by the said late husband endowed with life-tenure and dower in all his goods — on Tuesday immediately preceding had made a formal descent in person to the same Trąbczyn estate first, then to the villages of Osiny, Łazy, Nowa Wieś, the olędry, and the Huta belonging to it, then to the pine forests and woodlands pertaining to those same goods; and being everywhere throughout those same places in succession, in accordance with the form of law and custom, had duly viewed and inspected — to be entered as follows. Which aforesaid matters he attested before the said office as having duly viewed and inspected — of which he made and makes this his report in the present act.

[Translator's note: Szeptycki [Szepczyński]. Bartłomiej is named Szeptycki in this 1754 record and Szepczyński in the 1782 document; in the 1776 document he is uczciwy Bartłomi z Trąpczyna (the Honest Bartłomiej of Trąbczyn). All three designations refer to the same individual, who served as Court Summoner of Trąbczyn across at least the period 1754–1782. The variant spellings are preserved as written in their respective documents.]

[Translator's note: Life-tenure and dower. Dominae Reformatoriae et advitalitialis (Latin). Reformatoria denotes the right of a widow to reform or reclaim her dower on the death of her husband, a standard provision of Polish noble inheritance law. Advitalis denotes a life interest or life tenancy in the goods. Katarzyna Prusimska thus held both a dower-reform right and a life tenancy in all of Paweł Prusimski's goods.]

[Translator's note: Formal descent. Condescenderat (Latin, pluperfect of condescendere): a technical legal term denoting the formal act of proceeding to an estate for an official on-site inspection. The Tuesday in question was 9 July 1754 — three days before the registration on 12 July 1754 (the eve of the Feast of Saint Margaret, Virgin and Martyr).]

[Translator's note: 'To be entered as follows.' Utpote Inseratur (Latin): a formulaic note indicating that the content of the inspection — that is, Sections 1–3 above — is to be inserted into the court record at this point. The three Polish sections (building survey, tenant enumeration, and forest testimony) are thus the material being formally registered by this relatio.]
summary_en: The report of the court messenger Bartłomiej Szeptycki of Trąbczyn, entered in the records of the castle court at Konin on 12 July 1754, with the inspection he had made on 9 July at the request of Katarzyna Prusimska, born Rozdrażewska. She is the widow of Paweł Prusimski, the King's chamberlain and heir of Trąbczyn, who had died shortly before, and holds her dower and a life interest in all his estates. The inspection describes the buildings of the manor farm at Trąbczyn one by one: the old manor house is past repair and a new one stands finished in the frame; then come the kitchen, four barns, the sheepfold, the granary, the stables and sties, the distillery and the malthouse with their gear. At Nowa Wieś there are fifteen Olęder settlers, and the sixteenth plot is empty. A list counts the people who owe labour in Trąbczyn, Osiny, Łazy and Nowa Wieś as full farmers, half-farmers, cottagers and lodgers. Two noblemen, Kazimierz Świerczewski and Józef Puchalski, state over their signatures that in the pine woods of Trąbczyn, from Osiny to the Biskupice boundary and round Łazy, the better trees have been felled or picked out and only the leavings stand, and the same of the oaks, except where the Olęder settlers have taken the timber on their plots. The description of the village houses in the middle of the entry is not transcribed.
summary_de: Bericht des Gerichtsboten Bartłomiej Szeptycki von Trąbczyn, am 12. Juli 1754 in die Akten des Burggerichts Konin eingetragen, mit der Besichtigung, die er am 9. Juli auf Verlangen der Katarzyna Prusimska, geborene Rozdrażewska, vorgenommen hatte. Sie ist die Witwe des kurz zuvor verstorbenen Paweł Prusimski, königlichen Kämmerers und Erbherrn von Trąbczyn, und hat an allen seinen Gütern ihr Leibgedinge und ein lebenslanges Nutzungsrecht. Die Besichtigung beschreibt die Gebäude des Gutshofs in Trąbczyn eines nach dem anderen: Das alte Herrenhaus ist nicht mehr zu reparieren, ein neues ist im Rohbau fertig; es folgen Küche, vier Scheunen, Schafstall, Speicher, Ställe, Brennerei und Mälzerei mit ihrem Gerät. In Nowa Wieś sitzen fünfzehn Olęder, die sechzehnte Hufe ist leer. Eine Aufstellung zählt die dienstpflichtigen Leute in Trąbczyn, Osiny, Łazy und Nowa Wieś nach Vollbauern, Halbbauern, Häuslern und Einliegern. Zwei Adlige, Kazimierz Świerczewski und Józef Puchalski, bezeugen mit ihrer Unterschrift, dass in den Kiefernwäldern von Trąbczyn von Osiny bis zur Grenze von Biskupice und um Łazy die besseren Stämme gefällt oder herausgesucht sind und nur Ausschuss steht, ebenso bei den Eichen, außer wo die Olęder das Holz auf ihren Hufen genommen haben. Die Beschreibung der Dorfhäuser im mittleren Teil des Eintrags ist nicht transkribiert.
